newsitem.title: USA: Ford considers Russian auto plant.
newsitem.headline: Ford considers Russian auto plant.

text.p: Speaking at a conference on cross-border business alliances Tuesday, W. Wayne Booker, executive vice-president of Ford Motor Co in charge of emerging markets, said that company is considering a manufacturing facility in Russia.
"We are doing feasiblity studies to establish a manufacturing facility in Russia, which will probably be a joint-venture," said Booker.
He added that the project, if completed, might be done with private investors rather than a government entity, and may also involve a new facility.
Booker also said that Ford's current policy is to modify existing vehicles rather than introduce all-new designs in emerging markets.
Ford already has a manufacturing facility in Belarus, where European-model Escorts and Transits are scheduled to roll off the assmebly line in July.

In December, General Motors Corp began assembling Chevrolet Blazer sport/utility vehicles in Yelabuga, Russia, in the semi-autonomous region of Tartarstan. The factory will build about 10,000 vehicles annually from imported kits.

GM is scheduled to open a full-scale assembly line capable of bulding 45,000 vehicles a year in late 1998. It owns 25 percent equity in the Yelaz-GM joint venture, but has managment control, while the Russian and Tartar governments share a 75 percent stake.
